messages.author: 7c470552f98c92d3
messages.subject: Back transform error and AICcmodavg importance function error
parts:
Hi all,

I have been trying to complete a site use analysis for leopards using occupancy modelling and the AICcmodavg package, but have been having a couple of issues that I have yet to be able to resolve and I am hoping someone can point my amateur r understanding in the right direction! I have used code I used a few years ago for another study but now with a lot more models and obviously different data, it does not seem to be working as it did before, although I am very much expecting user error.

I have successfully run several models using the occu function, a lot more models than I will realistically want, but it was a bit of exploratory analysis. I have then taken the models that outperformed my null model as a new list, but in trying to back transform all of these a couple of them produce the below:
> backTransform(linearComb(Mod.TRAIL, coefficients = c(1,0), type = "state"))
Error in (function (cond)  :
  error in evaluating the argument 'obj' in selecting a method for function 'backTransform': ncol(coefficients) == length(est) is not TRUE

I have looked in the past chats in this group and seen a discussion about removing NA's as a result of factors to resolve this, but I was not sure that was applying to mine as it appears that the models with any of the covariates individually back transform successfully, suggesting that the data is workable with the function, but with a different combination there is more of an issue.

Possibly linked to this issue is for when I take a model that does run the back transform successfully and try to use the importance and modavg functions from the AICcmodavg package I get another error:
> importance(analysis_models, "Control", parm.type = "psi", c.hat = cHat, second.ord = TRUE)
Error in importance.AICunmarkedFitOccu(analysis_models, "Control", parm.type = "psi",  :
 
Parameter not found in any of the candidate models

I also get a blank response to using the evidence() function.

I have attached my code and files for reproduction in the link, and any help or guidance would be very appreciated! 

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1fsAkrliZMjdJx3fAcshRm3QBenxwMqpq?usp=sharing

Many thanks
Jamie

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] Back transform error and AICcmodavg importance function error
parts:
Dear Jamie,

 

I think backTransform() only works for Null models, i.e., those which have an intercept only. As soon as you have covariates, you need to use the predict function, which you can use to backtransform the intercept by setting the values of all covariates to zero.

 

Best regards  -- Marc

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Back transform error and AICcmodavg importance function error
parts:
Hi Jamie,

Regarding relative importance( ), you need to use the parm argument to
specify the variable name as it appears in the model output. For
example, if you have a Habitat variable with A, B, and C levels, you
could then write importance(parm = "HabitatB"), depending on the
reference level that was used in your model. This being said,
importance values are a "semi-quantitative" measure and can be of
limited value: you still need to inspect the output of the models
carefully, as a variable with high importance values might be
hitchhiking a ride in a model with a good predictor. Instead, you could
look at model-averaged predictions across your models vs the predictor
of interest.

Regarding evidence( ), the function requires the model selection table
as input.

Here is an example below illustrating both using an unmarked data set:

require(unmarked)
##single season example modified from ?occu
data(frogs)
pferUMF <- unmarkedFrameOccu(pfer.bin)
##add fake covariates
siteCovs(pferUMF) <- data.frame(sitevar1 = rnorm(numSites(pferUMF)),
sitevar2 = runif(numSites(pferUMF)))

##observation covariates
obsCovs(pferUMF) <- data.frame(obsvar1 = rnorm(numSites(pferUMF) *
obsNum(pferUMF)))

##basic model set
fm1 <- occu(~ obsvar1 ~ sitevar1, pferUMF)
fm2 <- occu(~ 1 ~ sitevar1, pferUMF)
fm3 <- occu(~ obsvar1 ~ sitevar2, pferUMF)
fm4 <- occu(~ 1 ~ sitevar2, pferUMF)

##assemble models in named list
CandMods <- list("fm1" = fm1, "fm2" = fm2, "fm3" = fm3, "fm4" = fm4)

##model selection table
modTable <- aictab(cand.set = Cand.mods, second.ord = TRUE)

##evidence ratio
evidence(modTable)

##relative importance of sitevar1
importance(cand.set = Cand.mods,
parm = "sitevar1", parm.type = "psi")


Hope it helps,

Marc

Hi all,

I have been trying to complete a site use analysis for leopards using occupancy modelling and the AICcmodavg package, but have been having a couple of issues that I have yet to be able to resolve and I am hoping someone can point my amateur r understanding in the right direction! Error in (function (cond) :

Jamie,

For evidence( ), the arguments "model.high" and "model.low" specify the
two models you want to compare. The default compares the top vs 2nd-
ranked model, but you can choose whichever pair of models you want.
Just specify the same name that you use in the model selection table to
refer to your models to get a comparison. Check the rownames of the
model selection table for the model names to use.

In your example of modavg( ), you should specify parm.type = "detect"
if your predictor is on detection probability. To get predictions, you
can use modavgPred( ).

Best,

Marc

> Hi Jamie,
>
> Regarding relative importance( ), you need to use the parm argument to
> specify the variable name as it appears in the model output. For
> example, if you have a Habitat variable with A, B, and C levels, you
> could then write importance(parm = "HabitatB"), depending on the
> reference level that was used in your model. This being said,
> importance values are a "semi-quantitative" measure and can be of
> limited value: you still need to inspect the output of the models
> carefully, as a variable with high importance values might be
> hitchhiking a ride in a model with a good predictor. Instead, you could
> look at model-averaged predictions across your models vs the predictor
> of interest.
>
> Regarding evidence( ), the function requires the model selection table
> as input.
>
> Here is an example below illustrating both using an unmarked data set:
>
> require(unmarked)
> ##single season example modified from ?occu
> data(frogs)
> pferUMF <- unmarkedFrameOccu(pfer.bin)
> ##add fake covariates
> siteCovs(pferUMF) <- data.frame(sitevar1 = rnorm(numSites(pferUMF)),
> sitevar2 = runif(numSites(pferUMF)))
>
> ##observation covariates
> obsCovs(pferUMF) <- data.frame(obsvar1 = rnorm(numSites(pferUMF) *
> obsNum(pferUMF)))
>
> ##basic model set
> fm1 <- occu(~ obsvar1 ~ sitevar1, pferUMF)
> fm2 <- occu(~ 1 ~ sitevar1, pferUMF)
> fm3 <- occu(~ obsvar1 ~ sitevar2, pferUMF)
> fm4 <- occu(~ 1 ~ sitevar2, pferUMF)
>
> ##assemble models in named list
> CandMods <- list("fm1" = fm1, "fm2" = fm2, "fm3" = fm3, "fm4" = fm4)
>
> ##model selection table
> modTable <- aictab(cand.set = Cand.mods, second.ord = TRUE)
>
> ##evidence ratio
> evidence(modTable)
>
> ##relative importance of sitevar1
> importance(cand.set = Cand.mods,
> parm = "sitevar1", parm.type = "psi")
>
>
> Hope it helps,

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Back transform error and AICcmodavg importance function error
parts:
In general as Marc says it is easier to use predict instead of backTransform and linearComb.

In your case the error is because you haven't provided the correct number of coefficients to linearComb for a few of the models. In your example Mod.TRAIL, there is only one state/occupancy parameter (the intercept) but in your code
backTransform(linearComb(Mod.TRAIL, coefficients = c(1,0), type = "state"))

You provide two parameter values. If you just change coefficients to c(1) it will work.

Ken
